Q1. Considering the following network with the given capacities
a. Use Ford-Fulkerson with DFS to compute the maximum flow from S to T. Show the augmenting paths used.
b. What is the worst-case time complexity of Ford-Fulkerson with DFS for this case?
c. For this case scenario is DFS perform poorly compared to BFS in finding augmenting paths? Justify your answer.

[DIAGRAM: Directed flow network with 4 nodes S, A, B, T and capacitated edges: S->A (10), S->B (5), A->B (15), A->T (10), B->T (5).]

document: Q2. As the project manager at a leading tech company, you are tasked with selecting and scheduling multiple short-term projects from various clients. Each project requires exactly one day to complete, offers a profit if finished on time, and has a strict deadline. Since only one project can be handled at a time, your objective is to maximize the total profit by prioritizing and scheduling the most profitable projects without missing any deadlines. Projects that cannot be completed within their deadline must be skipped. Given n projects, where each project is represented as a tuple (deadline, profit), develop an algorithmic approach and corresponding pseudocode to find the maximum possible profit and the optimal schedule of selected projects.

Q3. An e-commerce company generates sales report files for different products in varying sizes throughout the day. These reports need to be merged into a single comprehensive report for analysis. The merging cost is the sum of the sizes of the two reports being merged.
a. Give an algorithm to merge the files into a single file such that the merging cost is minimal.
b. You are given the following sales report files with their respective sizes (in MB). Calculate the minimum cost of merging the files into a single file.

| Sales Report | R1 | R2 | R3 | R4 | R5 | R6 | R7 | R8 |
| Size (in MB) | 5 | 8 | 3 | 6 | 2 | 9 | 4 | 7 |
